etymologies.etymologyHTML: Variant of chuck; or alternatively a diminutive of chump (“chunk; block”) +‎ *-k (diminutive suffix) (compare hunk from hump, etc.).

definitions.definition: A part of something that has been separated.

quote.text: Daylight, between mouthfuls, fed chunks of ice into the tin pot, where it thawed into water. ... Daylight cut up generous chunks of bacon and dropped them in the pot of bubbling beans.

definitions.definition: A representative portion of a substance, often large and irregular.
(linguistics, education) A sequence of two or more words that occur in language with high frequency but are not idiomatic; a bundle or cluster.
(computing) A discrete segment of a file, stream, etc. (especially one that represents audiovisual media); a block.

quote.citation: 1994, Paul J Perry, Multimedia developer's guide:
quote.text: The first DWORD of a chunk data in the RIFF chunk is a four character code value identifying the form type of the file.

definitions.definition: (comedy) A segment of a comedian's performance.

quote.citation: 1994, Gene Perret, Successful Stand-up Comedy: Advice from a Comedy Writer, page 80:
quote.text: You begin gathering two hours of dependable comedy by developing that first three-minute chunk. When you're satisfied with it, you create another three minutes of laughs, then another three minutes.

quote.citation: 2012, Jay Sankey, Zen and the Art of Stand-Up Comedy, page 168:
quote.text: If you're gigging outdoors for the Society of Catholic Gardeners, don't close your set with your "Papa Beelzebub" chunk (no matter how life affirming you think it is!).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To break into large pieces or chunks.
(transitive) To break down (language, etc.) into conceptual pieces of manageable size.

quote.citation: 2005, Yong Zhao, Research in Technology and Second Language Education:
quote.text: These results offer tentative evidence that suggests that certain components of computer-mediated instruction (in this case, access to and control over syntactically chunked, captioned video) are not necessarily beneficial for certain learners  […]

definitions.definition: (transitive, slang, chiefly Southern US) To throw.
(transitive, video games) Deal a substantial amount of damage to an opponent.
Archaic form of chank (“type of spiral shell”).
